title: Slide trombone, Ory, and dropping the violin from the Oliver band
summary: His uncle was first with the slide trombone; he recalls Ory and Oliver wanting a five-piece band modeled on the Dixieland Jazz Band, and his leaving the violin.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who was the first one really to play the slide trombone, as you say? Your uncle was the first one to do? My uncle. Doce Bonetta. Before that, they used mostly vowels. Vowels, that's all. When you were playing with Ori, was he playing slide or valve? Who? Kid Ori. Was that the other way? Ori always did use the slide, didn't he?
Ori? Yes. Yeah, Ori always did use the slide, since I started with Ori.
You think a lot later, of course, than Doceman.

Yeah, Ori always used the slide, since I knew him. I played with him. Well, slide was favorite then. It was all the vowels that was going out of style. Because Frank, he was never much on a slide. Well, Ori had a pretty good year for music. That's why Joe liked him so much. Catch on pretty quick. No, pretty quick. Also, Johnny. Johnny would catch on, make things, various from a violin like that, like piano and things like that. Johnny would catch it. He'd just bust out a laugh when he'd make it. And so, I went off to violins. We gave a job to a fellow, a band. Well, he was using seven pieces, you see. Give a job to a fellow. Joe did. And he went and played a job with six pieces. Well, when they hired Joe again, he says, listen, we're going to hire the band, but he says, how can't we have six pieces? We can't hear the violin much. So, this went on like that. So, this went on like that. When he said that, I quiff. Yeah, I quiff. So, when I quiff, he goes and get Barty Biggar's uncle, Emil, Biggar, to play a father. When I hear that rumor, I say, yeah, well, I'll get on the violinist for a stand. See, one band with me started the business off with six pieces. And the other fellow said, gee, that band sounds pretty good. Well, they wanted everybody to follow suit then. Joe and them hated that because they wanted me all the time. Because when they get a little tangled up with his music, I could show them his division all the time. Tell me, sir. And when they get on the piano or something, after Dixieland Jazz Band came up, using five pieces and things, well, Joe and Ori, they got crazy about that. They wanted to organize on that and follow the style of the Dixieland Band. And they hated to lose me because I could play the piano, too. But I did leave them from the violin.
